info.title: casefile
info.description:
The core's API (Bauplan §4). JSON in, JSON out; the surface is static files served beside it (ADR-014).

Every request leaves one audit line in `<root>/_audit/api.jsonl`. Identity is a signed cookie naming a
person from people.json; how it is obtained depends on the deployment (open in development and in the
demo sandbox, a login later). The core recovers half-done steps on start and records manual moves on read.

Two ways to run it:
- **one pipeline** (`Settings.root` + `config_dir`): the real thing, one store, one configuration;
- **the public demo** (`Settings.worlds`): every visitor gets a sandbox, a fresh copy of a world's template
  under `sessions_dir/<id>/`, bound to a signed cookie (ADR-016). "Start over" makes a new one. Old
  sandboxes are swept; a cap removes the oldest first; a per-IP limit protects the host.

post.description: The viewer's language, kept in a cookie for a year; only languages the domain's vocabulary speaks.
A fresh sandbox: start over, or switch to the other world.

get.description:
The demonstrations a sample workspace offers: whole flows the surface plays step by step. They travel with the
world they were written for (`_ablaeufe/*.json` in the template, put there by whoever built the world), so a flow
never meets data it does not fit.

post.description:
A sample workspace back to its world before a demonstration. Only where the shell named a world and its login lets
the person in; the public demo starts over with a fresh sandbox instead.
A new kind of case, copied from an existing one: a list entry and a format (domain/schemas.py).

Every case the viewer may read, as data: stage, meta, closing date, data point — for a client that keeps its
own commands (REQ-005 IF-04: `todo.py`). One read, no surface words.

Response List Cases Api Cases Get

post.description: A new case in the first stage, when the domain says how one starts (`theme.create`: label, roles, and what the meta carries).

get.description:
Home: in the demo every world the visitor has (their sandbox there, or the world as it starts); in a shell or a
single tree this workspace only; the surface asks the other workspaces of the shell itself, each at its own address.
A text file rendered for the viewer: {kind, html}. Images and PDFs come from /files.
An explainer from the application's configuration (`config/<domain>/videos/`); only files the catalog names.
What the pattern helper noticed across the files of this world: `_signale/*.md` at the pipeline root.

schema.title: Response Get Signals Api Signals Get

post.description:
A person moves a hint: looking into it, done (nothing to do, or handled), or back to open. The hint itself is never
changed or deleted; only its status, with who and when, in its header.

get.description: The house canon at one glance: every document by layer and depth, with scope, status, owner, origin.
One document of the house canon, rendered. Only files under `_kanon/`.
The rulebook of this world: read from the configuration and from `_bausteine/` at the pipeline root.

post.description: A change as a draft: a new version, or the open draft written over. A new id starts a new module.
The open draft comes into force; four eyes. Cases that started before keep the version they started with.
A proposed change not taken: it stays on record as rejected, with the reason. What was in force stays in force.
Out of force, as a version of its own with the reason. Nothing is deleted.
Start a list (id, name, the field it fills, whether a new case asks for it), or change one's name or asking.
Add an entry, or change one's name, colour, description or status. Written to the tree's lists.json, one line in _lists/log.jsonl.

Read or unread for the viewer alone (domain/seen.py). The surface sends it when a case is opened, and from
"Mark as unread". Not a step: nothing in the case changes.

"Show translation": the helper `translate` writes `<stem>.<lang>.md` beside the original, which stays as it
came. Once there, the same request answers at once. A background order: no thread entry, nobody's move.
The demo's 'put the sample invoice in': a bundled file lands in the slot as a delivered version.

put.description:
The on-site view's working state (theme.onsite.state), merged: a photo's view, a hint ticked or answered. State, not a
deliverable version — the photos and the note are the versioned files; this only says what they are and what is settled.

post.description: A mail dropped in by hand (.eml): the same way in as from the mailbox, so the demo and the real thing are one path.

AgainView.title: AgainView
AgainView.description:
A helper finished in this stage and the case did not move on: the viewer may send it again (SYS-161). An offer on
the case, not a move — it never counts in anybody's stack.

Entry.title: Entry
Entry.description: One item of the thread (review.md): `## REV-NNN — title`, a head line, text.

HelperView.title: HelperView
HelperView.description:
A helper at work on this case, as far as anybody can know: the phases its skill declares (run-policy `phases`), the
one it reached, what it does right now and just did — and how long such a run usually takes.

HomePlace.title: HomePlace
HomePlace.description: Home across workspaces (design hand-back, 2026-11-06): one workspace's part of the morning.

InterviewOut.title: InterviewOut
InterviewOut.description:
What one respondent sees of a conversation: the pack, their own answers and follow-ups, and how far everyone is.
Nobody sees another person's answers here; that is the outcome's business.

MatrixRow.title: MatrixRow
MatrixRow.description: One row of the rule matrix, in the viewer's words: when a mail is of this kind, this happens.

OnsiteIn.title: OnsiteIn
OnsiteIn.description: The assessor's state at the car: which view each photo shows, what they ticked or answered of the AI's hints.

OutcomeOut.title: OutcomeOut
OutcomeOut.description: The outcome: the findings, the draft with each line's decision, and the compiled canon when there is one.

PlaceOut.title: PlaceOut
PlaceOut.description: A workspace the person can be in, for the menu: its name, its colour and glyph (theme.app), whether it is this one.

RhythmOut.title: RhythmOut
RhythmOut.description:
What this person moved, honestly counted from the step journals: today and the last seven days. No streak, nothing
to lose — a rhythm to come back to.

RuleArea.title: RuleArea
RuleArea.description: An area a rule can apply to: a case label with its word and colour (the value list `label`).

RulesOut.title: RulesOut
RulesOut.description: The rulebook: stages and gates, what each helper does and never does, the approved modules and rules with versions, the connectors.

SetupOut.title: SetupOut
SetupOut.description: Setup (design hand-back, 2026-11-06): what this workspace is built from, read from its configuration.

SignalOut.title: SignalOut
SignalOut.description: A hint the pattern helper found across files: never a finding, always with its reasoning and the files it rests on.

Turn.title: Turn
Turn.description: One move that waits. Element 0 of `turn()` is the main one.
